fixes.result: Recheck original idle/absolute deadlines after UPDATE and before COMMIT; rollback credential generation and tombstone on expiry or clock failure, preserving the caller savepoint. Timely mutation remains valid if only COMMIT acknowledgement is delayed.
Reset successful-proof failure budgets with UPDATE, preserving the mutex row across a competing no-op INSERT / lock UPDATE acquisition.
fixes.classification: Availability / synchronization lifecycle; no authentication bypass demonstrated.
fixes.storage_impact: One budget/mutex row remains per used subject+purpose pair, including successful proofs. No TTL pruning; challenge cleanup does not delete mutex rows. SQL locks end with the transaction.

independent_review.scope: Independent read-only review of the final rotation expiry guard and OTP budget mutex retention change; production source was not edited by this reviewer.

rotation.changed_behavior: After successful conditional UPDATE and before transaction commit, re-evaluate the selected original row against a fresh clock; reject with the existing InvalidArgumentException when idle or absolute expiry has been reached.
rotation.atomicity: Existing transaction wrapper rolls back both new generation and old credential tombstone on guard rejection or a clock exception. Nested savepoint rejection preserves unrelated work in the caller transaction.
rotation.negative_control: A timely UPDATE followed by late commit acknowledgement remains accepted. Checking the original expiry after commit would reject an already timely rotation; retain the three reason-specific controls.
rotation.concurrent_touch: A touch committed after the initial SELECT can make the selected original deadline stale, so the guard can reject conservatively. The initial check already has this snapshot limitation; the contract does not guarantee rotation success across all simultaneous touches. No authentication extension is granted by this rejection.
rotation.locking_decision: Do not introduce FOR UPDATE or another SELECT for this confirmed expiry defect. Added locking would change contention/order semantics. In particular do not lock rowByUuid globally: it also serves isGrantCurrent and find.
rotation.phpstan_contract: The final @phpstan-impure annotation on now() accurately expresses advancing clock observations. It changes no PHP runtime behavior and avoids relying on repeated-call result caching in static analysis.

otp.changed_behavior: On successful challenge claim, reset failures to zero and window_started_at to the refreshed verification time by UPDATE while preserving the subject/purpose mutex row and lock_version.
otp.failure_path_addressed: Deleting the row after another operation has passed its INSERT ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING but before its mutex UPDATE can make that UPDATE affect zero rows and throw Could not acquire OTP budget lock. Retaining the row removes that deletion boundary for both issuance and verification.
otp.window_semantics: Success resets counters and starts a fresh fixed budget window at successful verification time. Old deletion recreated the window on a later acquire; retaining and explicitly resetting the window provides the promised successful-proof budget reset without erasing the mutex. Issuance already creates the initial window, so the contract does not promise anchoring every window to the first failed attempt.
otp.retention: At most one live row per distinct used subject_uuid/purpose pair under the composite primary key. This is a cardinality bound per pair, not a global storage bound or TTL purge. Challenge cleanup does not delete budget rows, as README now states. The retained row holds counters and coordination state, not OTP codes; the SQL row lock ends at transaction end.
otp.cleanup_recommendation: Do not add general expiry deletion of mutex rows as part of this patch: deleting rows while acquisitions are in flight would reintroduce the race. Any future subject-lifecycle purge needs explicit coordination.
otp.test_review: The tests exercise observable successful proof, budget reset, both pending-operation cases, and one-time consumption. Logger callback deterministically models an interleaving and asserts that the boundary was reached; it does not emulate native separate-connection contention.

finding.description: Successful verification deleted the subject/purpose mutex row after a competing issue/verify had completed its no-op INSERT, making the next lock UPDATE affect zero rows and throw.
finding.fix: Keep the mutex row and reset failures/window_started_at via UPDATE.
finding.evidence_boundary: Deterministic public Cycle driver logger schedules a second valid public verify between the first operation no-op INSERT and lock UPDATE, using SQLite to verify resulting state. PostgreSQL Read Committed schedule is supported by primary docs/source; native contention is not certified.
finding.storage_impact: One non-secret budget/mutex row persists per issued subject/purpose even after successful proof. Existing cleanup only prunes challenge history. Locks still release at transaction commit; counters reset on success; existing BIGINT lock_version schemas suffice.

root_contract_review.scope: Source review of subject/credential generation binding, authoritative factor gate, revocation after rotation, request publication ownership and observer isolation.
checks: Factor-management gate re-reads active session, checks UUID/subject/generation, bounds assurance age and invokes origin/token CSRF checks against authoritative state.
Tombstones do not authenticate and only permit revoking a successor during a stale logout; both live and tombstone lookups use the writer.
Rotation/touch use generation/CAS and existing rollback guards; subject-scoped revokeAll cannot revoke a different subject through exceptSessionId.
AuthenticationAdmission and SessionAuthenticationStrategy reject a provider identity whose UUID differs from the requested subject.
HTTP middleware drops previous concrete authentication state on denial or replacement; same-subject preserved state and candidate rollback follow documented ownership.
Observer and logger failures are isolated, while critical participants propagate failures before best-effort observation.
false_positive_filters: A request fabricated with both an identity and a denial attribute is outside the mutually exclusive states produced by built-in authentication middleware; it does not establish a reachable bypass.
Routing method and middleware selection remain the documented application integration responsibility. A direct invocation of an unregistered logout handler is not an application-level exploit proof.
No guarantee of distributed atomicity between validation, arbitrary user callbacks and later revocation was invented.
No supported built-in strategy was found to register pending publication and then return soft denial; a custom strategy doing so is not sufficient evidence against the default public flow.

scope: normal denial or fail-closed propagation on dependency failure
jwt_magic_password_webauthn_review.result: No new confirmed defect in the reviewed public paths.

auth-jwt: RefreshTokenManager validates bearer syntax before dispatch; DatabaseRefreshTokenStore serializes rotation and revocation through the family row, then rereads token state before claiming the old token.

Consumed nonexpired refresh proof compromises the complete family; family deadline caps every successor. JWT subject, issuer, audience, type and bounded evidence are checked before successful identity return.

RefreshHandler signs and allocates the response before rotation. Every fallible identity/guard/publication step after rotation is within the revocation compensation scope. TokenPairResponse also revokes a newly issued refresh grant if publication fails.
Revocation storage exceptions propagate as infrastructure failures. Access-token lifetime remains stateless as documented.
auth-magic-link: MagicLinkStrategy compares payload binding to the pre-authentication transaction before consuming purpose magic_link with the exact binding; returned identity UUID must equal the consumed record subject.

MagicLinkVerifyHandler verifies the browser proof, consumes that exact pre-authentication transaction, performs final admission and only then publishes a fresh session. The extractor and verification handler accept POST.

MagicLinkRequestHandler prepares response body before durable grant issuance. Queue or header-publication failure consumes the created pre-authentication grant; a delivered link cannot bypass that browser binding.
The strategy consumes the one-time bearer but never queues transport publication itself.
auth-password: PasswordStrategy uses the configured real verifier for both actual and dummy hashes, carries password/knowledge evidence and does not queue transport changes.
Browser login consumes its verified pre-authentication transaction before final session issue/publication. Final admission denial does not publish a session.

The reset service interface explicitly assigns consume/policy/password-change/long-lived-grant invalidation to the application service. The HTTP layer validates inputs and prepares success response before invoking that service.
Real Password2 controls reject a matching bcrypt prefix with an extra byte or NUL and accept the complete 72-byte value; stored Argon algorithms are honored.
auth-webauthn: Registration and authentication use separate ceremony types. Registration checks subject and returned user handle and consumes the ceremony before insert.

Authentication verifies with the stored public key through the real WebAuthn validator. Known-subject and discoverable user-handle rules are distinguished; subject and browser-binding checks precede session issue.

Commit consumes a ceremony once and updates only the credential matching ID, subject and expected counter. A deleted credential, different subject and stale counter do not update. Separate valid zero-counter assertions can update successfully.
Login requires a nonnull matching pre-authentication binding; reauthentication requires a null binding and the current subject. A final admission denial does not publish a session.

Crypto/parser rejection returns null or false; persistence exceptions outside the intentionally boolean registration insertion path propagate before any session issue. Option-publication failure consumes the exact pre-authentication grant.

discarded_candidates.candidate: Restore an old WebAuthn key after delete/reinsert of the same credential ID
discarded_candidates.decision: Not established as a defect of a supported public flow.
discarded_candidates.reason: A stale commit could only match a replacement if credential ID, subject and expected counter are deliberately reused while changing the key. W3C expects globally unique credential IDs, normal creation generates a new ID, and the existing primary key blocks live duplicate insertion. No real replacement workflow requiring such a collision was found. No artificial trusted-store mutation or new CAS API was introduced.

discarded_candidates.candidate: Reject every second zero-counter WebAuthn update using storage revision
discarded_candidates.reason: Independent single-use ceremonies may legitimately use authenticators with zero counters. The documented revision is a changed-row storage mechanism, not an authentication sequence token.

discarded_candidates.candidate: Refresh store must use a fresh internal clock after every blocking operation
discarded_candidates.decision: Out of the stated store contract.
discarded_candidates.reason: Public methods explicitly receive the caller-selected now; no live-clock guarantee or new clock dependency was invented.

discarded_candidates.candidate: Reset HTTP handler must atomically consume proof and revoke sessions
discarded_candidates.decision: Owned by the application reset service.
discarded_candidates.reason: PasswordResetServiceInterface explicitly assigns the complete transition to that implementation.

discarded_candidates.candidate: Authenticator needs checkpoints between these built-in strategy attempts
discarded_candidates.decision: No supporting built-in publication path found.
discarded_candidates.reason: JWT, Magic Link and Password strategies do not publish credential transport state before denial or success. An arbitrary custom strategy capable of mutation was not treated as a supported exploit.

discarded_candidates.candidate: Public attempt DTO construction or borrowed nested claims bypass validation
discarded_candidates.decision: Trusted application ownership, not a new external proof-validation defect.
discarded_candidates.reason: No new universal deep-copy or nonconstructible proof-token contract was imposed.

primary_sources_consulted.used_for: Assess the credential replacement hypothesis and credential-ID lifecycle, not a claim that arbitrary reused IDs are cryptographically impossible.

limitations: The 75 targeted existing tests verify the reviewed paths; this is not a repeated broad compatibility gate. Root owns the final whole-family PHP 8.4/8.5 verification.
Database behavior here uses SQLite and existing deterministic test drivers; no native MySQL/PostgreSQL concurrency claim is made.
WebAuthn controls use local cryptographically valid signed assertion fixtures, not physical authenticator or browser interoperability tests.
No new RED/GREEN pair was created because no new supported-contract defect was confirmed.

otp_totp_recovery_remember_review.method: Bounded read-only source and public-contract review. Existing test names were inspected as coverage context; no new tests or probes were executed in this subtask.

checks.conclusion: Verifier includes challenge UUID and configured purpose. Store checks the supplied binding and atomically claims only an unconsumed challenge. Login binding comes from the verified pre-authentication transaction; reauthentication uses the current session UUID and checks both session/identity and result/identity subjects. New issue invalidates unconsumed challenges for the same subject, purpose and binding. Revoke retains issuance history.

A delivery exception invokes revoke on the exact issued challenge. A request publication/queue exception consumes its exact pre-authentication grant. These paths do not promise atomicity across independently failing delivery, database and response systems.

checks.invariant: Subject binding, pending replacement and disable
checks.conclusion: Authenticated-encryption associated data includes the subject UUID. Enrollment replaces pending fields without disabling the active factor. Activation claims the exact pending ciphertext; verification conditions include subject, active ciphertext/key/nonce and previous replay step. Disable deletes the entire subject row, including pending and active credentials. Operations linearized before a later disable are not required to be undone.

Enrollment handlers call the authoritative-session, bounded-assurance and CSRF guard before mutation. Reauthentication requires the presented identity and session to have the same subject. TOTP is a subject-bound factor; it does not promise that each numeric code is bound to one browser or HTTP purpose.

checks.invariant: Subject isolation, regenerate/revoke and single consumption
checks.conclusion: Consumption matches subject plus canonical code hash and unused state. Regeneration and revokeAll hold the durable subject lock; batch deletion/insertion is transactional. A successful consume before regeneration can linearize before it; an old batch is absent after regeneration. Duplicate regeneration responses may contain a superseded batch as explicitly documented. The HTTP regeneration guard precedes mutation.

Rotation claims selector/verifier/generation; binding also matches subject and previous session, with a writer-read idempotency check for an already bound generation. revokeRotation is generation-scoped, while revokeCredential intentionally revokes the stable selector and its successors. Session and subject revocations use their declared scopes. Logout clears the pending transport and revokes the linked/presented grant before invoking session logout.

checks.invariant: Soft denial cannot retain strategy-owned publication compensation
checks.conclusion: Every continueOnFailure=true path precedes onDiscard registration. Missing/mismatched identity after rotation revokes that rotation before soft denial; failed revocation throws instead of returning a soft denial. After onDiscard registration, the strategy has only the successful AuthenticationResult return. The strategy itself never queues a publication. Deferred grant and session publication have request-owner discard compensation.

considered_but_not_promoted.candidate: OTP verified and consumed pre-authentication UUID are not compared again
considered_but_not_promoted.reason: The concrete DatabasePreAuthenticationManager binds the same immutable request credential/request-token pair to one UUID and has no public operation that reassigns that pair. Demonstrating a mismatch would require a nonconforming adapter, mutable request outside PSR expectations, or out-of-band storage tampering; no supported path was found.

considered_but_not_promoted.candidate: Counting an invalid OTP submission after a concurrent consumption/revocation
considered_but_not_promoted.reason: The stale-read branch can still record an aggregate failed submission after its conditional per-challenge update affects no row. This does not admit a proof; no public promise was found that aggregate failed-submission counts exclude such attempts. No speculative concurrency test or change was added.

considered_but_not_promoted.candidate: Previously accepted proof is not restored after a later downstream failure
considered_but_not_promoted.reason: Single-use proofs intentionally remain consumed after later admission/publication failure. Cross-resource atomicity or restoring a spent proof is not a declared guarantee. Response loss after TOTP enrollment or recovery batch regeneration is not treated as an authentication bypass.

considered_but_not_promoted.candidate: Manually forged rotation state or imported/corrupted rows
considered_but_not_promoted.reason: Trusted manager/state interfaces and direct database write access are not HTTP proof boundaries. No new inconsistency beyond the previously fixed TOTP metadata validation was established.

No new behavioral tests, mutation run, native PostgreSQL/MySQL concurrency run or write-failure probe was performed in this subtask.
Earlier expiry, OTP mutex-retention and TOTP persisted-metadata fixes were not presented as new findings or freshly rerun evidence.
The root agent independently owns the final PHP 8.5/PHP 8.4 package matrix and report/publication verification.
Lifecycle claims assume the bundled adapters, valid schemas, configured trust boundaries, and ordinary database transaction semantics; no undeclared distributed atomicity is inferred.
